summary.text: Nathalia Fernandez is the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for re-election to New York State Senate District 34, which covers the east Bronx and part of southern Westchester County. A former legislative aide and staff member in the office of Governor Andrew Cuomo, she won a 2018 special election to the State Assembly, represented Assembly District 80 until 2023, and has been a state senator since January 2023. She chairs the Senate Alcoholism and Substance Use Disorders Committee.

paragraphs.text: Fernandez was born in 1988, according to Wikipedia, to a father who immigrated from Cuba and a mother who immigrated from Colombia; she grew up in Rockland and then Westchester County and graduated from North Salem High School. In her 2022 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she describes herself as a daughter of immigrants whose father started and ran a small business.
She earned a B.A. in public relations from Hofstra University in 2010.
Before running for office, she worked as an administrative assistant at Genesis Realty Group and as an executive coordinator and chief of staff to Assemblymember Mark Gjonaj.
Fernandez served as a Bronx regional representative in the office of Governor Andrew Cuomo; Wikipedia dates her start in that role to 2017.

She won an April 24, 2018 special election for the 80th Assembly District, the seat vacated by Gjonaj after he won a New York City Council seat, defeating Republican Gene DeFrancis. She was re-elected in 2018 and 2020 and represented the district until moving to the State Senate.

In 2022 she said she co-chaired the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus's Subcommittee on Minority and Women-Owned Enterprise & Economic Development and had passed the Andrew Kearse Act, which requires that people in police custody be given medical attention if needed.
Fernandez took office in the State Senate on January 1, 2023, succeeding Alessandra Biaggi, and the nysenate.gov biography describes her as the first Latina to represent the 34th Senate District.

She co-chairs the Joint Senate Task Force on Opioids, Addiction and Overdose Prevention, and her other committee assignments include Agriculture, Cannabis, Insurance, Labor, Mental Health, Rules and Transportation.
A 2022 Bronx Times profile listed her residence as Morris Park.
